criteria.rationale: Inspected the sealed L1/L2 declarations, parser, plan/bundle sealing and conclusion gate. Composite limit attribution and post-seal behavior are verified; L1's author-written scope and L2's post-seal edit boundary are disclosed and justified residual risks. The reason parser defect means R4 does not reliably separate justified assumptions from unsupported ones.

Reviewed the added parsing and conclusion flow: this change adds immutable review data and no shared mutable state, asynchronous work, or new cancellation/lifecycle path. The sealed pose-mcp unit suite passes.
The new review-brief/11 contract carries the sealed limit and finding attribution, while empty optional fields remain omitted. The sealed integration contract test passes.

The plan, bundle, brief and attestation consumers are connected through the existing review flow. The integration assessment's unobserved HTTP consumers are outside these changed review-limit paths; the sealed bundle-convergence integration passes.
Parser failures return a specific accepted-limit diagnostic and the conclusion gate returns a blocker naming an unsealed limit or missing rationale. The sealed pose-mcp unit suite passes.

The brief contract advances to version 11; new fields are omitted when empty, preserving prior plan and bundle serialization, and ADR coverage was updated for qualified IDs. Reviewed the version/digest tests and the sealed immutable-template integration.

R1 is implemented by parsing once and sealing accepted limits in the plan and bundle; R2 exposes that snapshot in brief v11; R3 records a distinct within-limit disposition; R4 checks reasons and ADR references. D1 assigns semantic scope judgment to the reviewer and requires a sealed ID plus rationale; D2 binds the limits to the plan digest and omits empty fields. The design assessment reported no structural deltas.

Reviewed English and Portuguese manual/scaffold copies against runtime behavior: the documents describe the v11 sealed limits and qualified IDs consistently; the sealed template parity integration passes.
The implementation stays within accepted-limit parsing, review-plan/bundle sealing, brief, conclusion and readiness lint behavior named by the spec. The design assessment found no structural deltas.

Reviewed the input and authority boundary. A within-limit finding must name an ID sealed in that bundle and carry a rationale; an unsealed ID blocks approval. D1 leaves whether a finding semantically falls within a limit to the reviewer, and the brief exposes the declared limit for that judgment. No path or new authority input is introduced.

A shared parser and optional plan/bundle fields are the smallest sufficient path to carry the same declared limit through readiness, review and closeout; the v11 template makes the new reviewer decision explicit. Omitting empty fields preserves old digests. A documentation-only alternative would not seal or validate the limit. D1 would need reconsideration if semantic membership were required to be machine-proven rather than reviewer-judged; that is not this spec's choice.

findings.action: The accepted-limit reason regex treats punctuation-only text such as '..' as a reason, allowing an unjustified limit through ready-check, and rejects a valid reason beginning with a one-character token. R4's justification gate can therefore false-pass.
